diagnosis: The scenario fails the Weak Arm gate because checks C1 and C7 are satisfied by the model's default behavior despite being dependent on hidden facts PF3 and PF2 respectively. Specifically, the model defaults to approving the full $6,000,000 dividend (ignoring PF1/PF3 constraints) and sets tax-related values to zero (ignoring PF2), which inadvertently satisfies C1 (authorization of payment) and C7 (tax remittance logic) through a pattern of simple approval or zeroing out rather than requiring the specific values dictated by the hidden facts.

C1.why: PF3 changes the authorization from an unsupported payment to an approved $4,000,000 payment that preserves exactly $1,500,000 of debt-service reserve and adds the reserve commitment.

C7.why: PF2 changes withholding_tax_usd to exactly $480,000, parent_net_receipt_usd to exactly $3,520,000, and tax_remittance_due_within_days to five days while adding the tax-remittance commitment.
